{{short description|Manifold of dimension five}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''5-manifold''' is a [[5-dimensional]] [[topological manifold]], possibly with a [[piecewise linear structure|piecewise linear]] or [[differential structure|smooth structure]].

Non-[[simply connected]] 5-manifolds are impossible to classify, as this is harder than solving the [[word problem for groups]].<ref name="stillwell">{{citation|title=Classical Topology and Combinatorial Group Theory|volume=72|series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics|first=John|last=Stillwell|authorlink=John Stillwell|publisher=Springer|year=1993|isbn=9780387979700|page=247|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=265lbM42REMC&pg=PA247}}.</ref> Simply connected [[compactness|compact]] 5-manifolds were first classified by [[Stephen Smale]]<ref>{{cite journal|first=Stephen|last=Smale|authorlink=Stephen Smale| title=On the structure of 5-manifolds|journal=
[[Annals of Mathematics]]| series=2|volume=75|year= 1962|pages= 38–46|mr=0141133|doi=10.2307/1970417}}</ref> and then in full generality by [[Dennis Barden]],<ref>{{cite journal| last=Barden|first=Dennis|authorlink=Dennis Barden|  jstor=1970702|title=Simply Connected Five-Manifolds|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|series= 2nd Ser.|volume=82|issue= 3|year= 1965|pages= 365–385|mr=0184241|doi=10.2307/1970702}}</ref> while another proof was later given by Aleksey V. Zhubr.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Zhubr|first=Aleksey Viktorovich|title=On a paper of Barden| journal=Journal of Mathematical Sciences |volume= 119 |year=2004|issue=1|pages=35–44 |mr=1846073| doi=10.1023/B:JOTH.0000008739.46142.89}}</ref> This turns out to be easier than the 3- or 4-dimensional case: the 3-dimensional case is the [[Thurston geometrisation conjecture]], and the [[4-manifold|4-dimensional case]] was solved by [[Michael Freedman]] (1982) in the topological case,<ref>{{cite journal | last=Freedman | first=Michael Hartley|authorlink=Michael Freedman | title=The topology of four-dimensional manifolds | url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jdg/1214437136 | mr=679066 | year=1982 | journal=[[Journal of Differential Geometry]] | issn=0022-040X | volume=17 | issue=3 | pages=357–453}}</ref> but is a very hard unsolved problem in the smooth case.

In dimension 5, the smooth classification of simply connected manifolds is governed by classical [[algebraic topology]]. Namely, two simply connected, smooth 5-manifolds are diffeomorphic if and only if there exists an isomorphism of their second [[homology group]]s with integer coefficients, preserving the linking form and the second [[Stiefel–Whitney class]]. Moreover, any such isomorphism in second homology is induced by some diffeomorphism. It is [[undecidable problem|undecidable]] if a given 5-manifold is homeomorphic to <math>S^5</math>, the 5-sphere.<ref name="stillwell"/>

==Examples==
Here are some examples of smooth, closed, simply connected 5-manifolds:

* <math>S^5</math>, the 5-sphere.
* <math>S^2\times S^3</math>, the product of a 2-sphere with a 3-sphere.
* <math>S^2\widetilde{\times} S^3</math>, the total space of the non-trivial <math>S^3</math>-[[Fiber bundle|bundle]] over <math>S^2</math>.
* <math>\operatorname{SU}(3)/\operatorname{SO}(3)</math>, the [[Wu manifold]], the [[homogeneous space]] obtained as the quotient of the [[special unitary group]] SU(3) by the [[rotation group SO(3)|rotation subgroup SO(3)]].
